title: Change-set commit + optimistic retry protocol for batching/caching recommendations
creator: Leah Martinez
description:
Problem: Optimize automation needs an API/SDK primitive that lets control-plane and platform consumers safely propose, preview, commit, and if necessary rollback batching/caching configuration changes for Dedicated/Private deployments without risking duplicate or partially-applied recommendations. Existing endpoints are ad-hoc (suggestions -> apply) and rely on callers to dedupe, which has led to double-apply incidents and confusing retries under network flakiness.

Proposal: introduce a change-set-based protocol ("change-set") that encapsulates one or more recommendations (batching window, KV cache TTLs, quantization profile toggles) plus preconditions. The protocol provides: dry-run preview, persistent server-side change-set store, commit endpoint which is idempotent via client-provided idempotency token, webhook acknowledgements for async apply, and a reconcile endpoint for exactly-once semantics via optimistic retry and monotonic operation IDs. The server keeps an immutable operation log per change-set to enable rollforward or compensating rollback.

Key API sketch (v1):
- POST /optimize/change-sets      -> create change-set (body: changes[], preconditions[], client_token) returns change_set_id, status=created
- POST /optimize/change-sets/{id}/preview -> run dry-run (no mutation), returns preview diff, cost delta estimate, risk score
- POST /optimize/change-sets/{id}/commit  -> commit apply request, idempotent, accepts client_token if not supplied at create time; returns operation_id and apply_state (queued|applying|applied|failed)
- GET  /optimize/change-sets/{id}/status  -> fetch current status, operation log, timestamps
- POST /optimize/change-sets/{id}/rollback -> create compensating change-set (link back to original), returns rollback_change_set_id
- Webhook: /webhooks/optimize/events (subscribers register with callback and secret) sends events: change_set.created, preview.completed, commit.started, commit.finished (success|failure), rollback.created, rollback.finished
- POST /optimize/change-sets/{id}/reconcile -> reconciliation endpoint for callers that observed webhook failure; accepting last_known_operation_id to continue from last applied op

Idempotency and safety rules:
- client_token is required for commit-level idempotency; server uses (change_set_id, client_token) pair to dedupe commit attempts and return the same operation_id for retries.
- server enforces optimistic preconditions (model_version, dedicated_pool_id, current_config_hash). If a precondition fails the commit returns 409 with a diff and suggested resolution.
- operations are recorded in an append-only operation log: create -> preview -> commit:start -> commit:complete -> rollback:start -> rollback:complete. This enables deterministic replay and crash recovery.
- rollback is implemented as a compensating change-set that reverses the recorded operations; rollbacks are also idempotent and recorded in the operation log.

Acceptance criteria:
1) API endpoints implemented and documented in SDKs (Python/TypeScript).
2) Server persists change-sets + operation logs and survives restarts (integration test proves restart + reconcile).
3) Webhook delivery supports at-least-once semantics and includes operation_id for deduplication on the subscriber side.
4) Commit endpoint returns identical operation_id on retries within 7 days with same client_token.
5) End-to-end integration tests with Dedicated autoscaler reproduce failure modes (network drop, leader failover) and verify no double-applies.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer optimistic concurrency (precondition checks) over distributed locks to avoid global coordination; trade-off: clients must handle 409 and either refresh or reconcile.
- Keeping an immutable operation log increases storage but simplifies correctness and postmortem analysis; we will TTL logs after 90 days (configurable).
- Webhook delivery will be at-least-once; subscribers must dedupe using operation_id and change_set_id. We'll provide a helper SDK function for safe webhook handlers.

Risks:
- Complexity for clients to adopt new protocol (we will provide migration guide and a convenience endpoint that wraps create+commit for simple use cases).
- Rollbacks are compensating and may not be perfectly reversible if downstream systems mutate in unexpected ways; add audit and manual rollback flows for high-risk customers.

Related artifacts: confluence and design links in attachments.
